7.title: Build a pedestrian crossing
7.intro: Continue your own Arduino IDE traffic-light sketch. Add pedestrian lights and a request button.
goals: Make traffic stop before pedestrians get green.
Use a button to request a crossing.

stages.title: Continue your traffic lights

learn.text: Your existing Arduino commands control the car lights: red 8, amber 9, green 10.
3000 milliseconds is 3 seconds. Keep your own working code.

steps: Open your own Week 6 .ino in Arduino IDE. Save a Week 7 copy.
Finish green for 3 seconds, amber for 1 second, then red for 1 second.
Run it. Switch each light off before the next starts.
stages.result: Your three car lights run green → amber → red, with only one on.
stages.hint: Still on one LED? Keep its on–wait–off commands. Add the same commands for the other two.
stages.teacherQuestion: What working code can you keep? Which command turns the previous light off?
stages.teacherWatch: Help unfinished learners get one clear three-light sequence. Use the diagram to check pins before changing code.

stages.title: Add the crossing circuit

learn.text: Each LED needs its own 330Ω resistor. Connect its A side through the resistor to its output, and C to GND.
Set both new pedestrian pins as outputs in setup(). During normal traffic, pedestrian red stays on and green stays off.
The supplied helper prepares the button. Pressed reads LOW; released reads HIGH. You do not need to write the button-reading code.

steps: Save your own .ino first. Use setup help to place crossing.h and crossing.cpp beside your Week 7 .ino.
Follow the labelled diagram to add two pedestrian LEDs and the button. Wokwi is an optional circuit tester.
In Arduino IDE, add both pedestrian outputs in setup(). Start pedestrian red on and green off.
stages.result: You have five connected LEDs and a button. Pedestrian red is on during normal traffic.
stages.hint: Keep the .ino, crossing.h and crossing.cpp in one sketch folder. Match the diagram: car pins 8/9/10, pedestrian pins 6/7, button pin 2.
stages.teacherQuestion: Which pedestrian light tells people to wait? Trace one LED back to GND.
stages.teacherWatch: Check separate resistors, LED A/C polarity and button-to-GND wiring. Do not replace the learner’s own sketch.

stages.title: Remember a button request

learn.text: Add this above setup(). crossing.h and crossing.cpp are supplied files beside your .ino, not a library to install.
Call this once inside setup() to prepare the button.
Replace every delay with Crossing.pause using the same milliseconds. It remembers a tap of at least 0.1 seconds during waits.

steps: Add the include line and call Crossing.begin() in setup().
Replace every normal delay(...) with Crossing.pause(...). Keep the same times.
Find the checkpoint after car red has waited 1 second. This is where your request decision goes next.
stages.result: Your traffic sequence still works. Its waits can now remember a button request.
stages.hint: A plain delay cannot check the button while it waits. Use the supplied pause helper for all waits.
stages.teacherQuestion: Why might a quick tap be missed during an ordinary delay? Where is our safe checkpoint?
stages.teacherWatch: Check all waits use the helper. A request waits for the red checkpoint; it must not turn pedestrian green on immediately.

stages.title: Write the crossing decision

learn.text: At the red checkpoint, run a crossing only if a request is waiting. Put your crossing commands inside this block.
Put beginCrossing at the start and endCrossing at the end. The helper ignores presses during a crossing and prevents a held button repeating it.
These are the pedestrian green commands. They are only parts of your sequence, not a complete crossing.

steps: At the red checkpoint, add the request if block. Begin the crossing; keep car red on, car amber/green off and pedestrian red on. Wait 1 second.
Turn pedestrian red off and green on. Wait 5 seconds using the helper.
Turn pedestrian green off and red on. Wait 1 second with cars still red, then end the crossing and resume your traffic sequence.
stages.result: A remembered request stops cars before pedestrians get green. Without a request, normal traffic continues.
stages.hint: Never leave car green on with pedestrian green. Keep every crossing command inside the if block and close it with }.
stages.teacherQuestion: Which lights must be off before pedestrians get green? What happens if nobody presses?
stages.teacherWatch: Test the two all-red pauses and pedestrian red during normal traffic. Arduino loop() keeps the controller running.

project.title: Test your crossing
project.brief: Use your own traffic controller to serve one remembered pedestrian request safely.
requirements: Normal: car green 3 seconds → amber 1 → red 1; pedestrian red stays on.
At the red checkpoint: all red 1 second → pedestrian green 5 → pedestrian red and car red 1, then resume.
Remember a tap during waits. Ignore presses during the crossing; a held button must not repeat it.
tests: Tap for at least 0.1 seconds during a normal wait. It may take up to 5 seconds to reach the red checkpoint, then 1 all-red second before pedestrian green.
Watch a complete crossing. Car green and pedestrian green must never be on together.
Hold the button through a crossing, then release it. It must not start another crossing until a new tap.
project.teacherQuestion: How can you show the request was remembered without letting pedestrians go too soon?
project.teacherWatch: Try green-, amber- and red-phase taps, no request and a held button. Check every wait uses Crossing.pause.

exit: How did your program keep the two green lights apart?
What should happen if the button is held down?

8.title: Build a pedestrian crossing
8.intro: Continue your own traffic-light program. Add pedestrian lights and a request button.
goals: Make traffic stop before pedestrians get green.
Use a button to request a crossing.

stages.title: Continue your traffic lights

learn.text: Keep your own Pin outputs: red GP15, amber GP16 and green GP17.
Use this complete supplied repeat line. Keep your traffic sequence indented below it.

steps: Open your own Week 6 project. Save a copy for Week 7.
Finish green for 3 seconds, amber for 1 second, then red for 1 second.
Run three rounds. Switch each light off before the next starts.
stages.result: Your three car lights run green → amber → red, with only one on.
stages.hint: Still on one LED? Keep its on–wait–off commands. Add the same commands for the other two.
stages.teacherQuestion: What working code can you keep? Which command turns the previous light off?
stages.teacherWatch: Help unfinished learners get one clear three-light sequence. Supply the complete range line; no other loop form is needed.

stages.title: Add the crossing circuit

learn.code: Pedestrian red: GP18 · green: GP19 · button: GP20 → GND
learn.text: Each LED needs its own 330Ω resistor. Connect its A side through the resistor to its output, and C to GND.

learn.code:
ped_red = Pin(18, Pin.OUT)
ped_green = Pin(19, Pin.OUT)
learn.text: Prepare the pedestrian outputs. During normal traffic, pedestrian red stays on and green stays off.
The supplied helper prepares the button. Pressed reads 0; released reads 1. You do not need to write the button-reading code.

steps: Save your own main.py first. Download and unzip the Week 7 student files.
In your Wokwi file menu, upload diagram.json and crossing.py. Keep your own main.py.
Add the two pedestrian outputs. Start pedestrian red on and green off.
stages.result: You have five connected LEDs and a button. Pedestrian red is on during normal traffic.
stages.hint: Compare the labelled diagram. Keep car red GP15, amber GP16 and green GP17. The helper sets up button GP20.
stages.teacherQuestion: Which pedestrian light tells people to wait? Trace one LED back to GND.
stages.teacherWatch: Check separate resistors, LED A/C polarity and button-to-GND wiring. Do not replace the learner’s own main.py.

stages.title: Remember a button request

learn.text: Keep the built-in Pin import for your outputs. Nothing to install.

learn.code: from crossing import pause, requested, begin_crossing, end_crossing
learn.text: crossing.py is the supplied local helper file. Keep it beside main.py.
Replace every sleep with pause using the same seconds. It remembers a tap of at least 0.1 seconds during waits.

steps: Add the crossing import at the top of main.py. Keep the Pin import.
Replace every normal sleep(...) with pause(...). Keep the same times.
Find the checkpoint after car red has waited 1 second. This is where your request decision goes next.
stages.result: Your traffic sequence still works. Its waits can now remember a button request.
stages.hint: A plain sleep cannot check the button while it waits. Use the supplied pause helper for all waits.

stages.teacherWatch: Check all waits use the helper. A request waits for the red checkpoint; it must not turn pedestrian green on immediately.

stages.title: Write the crossing decision

learn.text: At the red checkpoint, run a crossing only if a request is waiting. Indent your crossing commands below this line.
Put begin_crossing at the start and end_crossing at the end. The helper ignores presses during a crossing and prevents a held button repeating it.
These are the pedestrian green commands. They are only parts of your sequence, not a complete crossing.

steps: At the red checkpoint, add the request if. Begin the crossing; keep car red on, car amber/green off and pedestrian red on. Wait 1 second.
Turn pedestrian red off and green on. Wait 5 seconds using the helper.
Turn pedestrian green off and red on. Wait 1 second with cars still red, then end the crossing. After three rounds, finish with both reds on and all other lights off.
stages.result: A remembered request stops cars before pedestrians get green. The three-round test finishes with both reds on.
stages.hint: Never leave car green on with pedestrian green. Keep crossing commands inside the if, within your supplied range block.
stages.teacherQuestion: Which lights must be off before pedestrians get green? What happens if nobody presses?
stages.teacherWatch: Test the two all-red pauses and pedestrian red during normal traffic. This test runs three rounds; Stop then Run starts it again.
